newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court opens security scandal murder case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court opens security scandal murder case.

text.p: A Turkish court on Tuesday began the trial of five men, four of them policemen, accused of taking part in the murder of a leading casino entrepreneur linked to a high-profile security scandal.
State-run Anatolian news agency said the men were charged with participation in the killing of "Casino King" Omer Lutfu Topal, found shot dead in his car in July last year.

Media reports have said three of the policemen, bodyguards of MP Sedat Bucak, killed Topal in a battle over laundered money from the heroin trade. Topal was alleged to have given money to Kurdish separatist rebels.
The four "special team" policemen are also on trial on a separate charge of forming an armed gang that threatened state security.
The security scandal erupted last November after a car crash near the western town of Susurluk which killed a wanted right-wing gangster, a top policeman and a former beauty queen.
Bucak, who heads an anti-rebel Kurdish militia, was in the same car but survived.
Bucak's three bodyguards, travelling in another car behind the crash vehicle at the time, are also accused of concealing from authorities the whereabouts of the gangster Abdullah Catli.
Catli was wanted for the killing of seven left-wing students in a bomb attack in 1978.
The accident spurred a series of reports that painted a picture of gangsters using state privileges and political connections to kill opponents, trade drugs and traffic in guns.
A former interior minister resigned after being implicated in the affair. He and Bucak are protected from prosecution by parliamentary immunity.
